policy: Archived implementations do not claim live acceptance. These are observation, operator-input or revisit items linked to archived records; they do not hold implementation closure.

items.title: Visual-builds PostgreSQL proof and recovery wiring
items.detail: The 013A design requires tests/visual-builds-store.test.mjs in scripts/postgres-concurrency-proof.mjs and showcase.assets/revisions in scripts/db-recovery-drill.mjs. The test and schema do not exist, so adding the path now would fail the mandatory test:postgres gate. This record is not proof that the concurrency or recovery proof ran.
items.next_action: When 013A schema/store lands, add tests/visual-builds-store.test.mjs to TEST_FILES, extend the recovery drill to seed and compare showcase asset/revision hashes, then run npm run test:postgres, npm run test:recovery and npm run verify:supabase.

items.title: Account email sender, disclosure and controlled inbox acceptance
items.detail: Verification/recovery implementation is tested against a local Resend-shaped endpoint. No operator sender, sending credential or controlled inbox has been supplied. Published policy v1.1 does not name the new email recipient; approval of a new immutable privacy version is required before real delivery is enabled. A provider acceptance id is not proof of inbox receipt.
items.next_action: Approve the recipient disclosure under FID-061, select/provision the sender and transport with credentials outside the tree, authorize a controlled verification/recovery message, and record actual inbox receipt, consumed links, replay refusal and revoked sessions/keys against the pinned artifact.

items.title: Hosted ingress identity and resource-boundary acceptance
items.detail: Local production HTTP proves byte/schema/issuance/account limits. No hosted ingress exists for proxy header stripping, slow/large transport behavior, timeout/SSE cancellation or restart observations. The default ignores forwarded headers and shares one untrusted-client bucket; selecting a header requires a controlled ingress that strips and sets it.
items.next_action: After explicit deployment approval, configure the trusted ingress header, prove clients cannot forge it or bypass the proxy, and record size/time/cancel/restart receipts against the pinned artifact. Limiter state resets on process restart; the supported topology remains one process.

items.title: Live upstream capacity under the 15 rpm fallback
items.detail: The free-path fix was verified against the mock provider only. The real 15 rpm fallback and the provider's /balance cadence under load were not exercised.
items.next_action: On the next live call pass, measure the fallback and the account-check cadence against the real upstream account.

items.title: Probe coverage beyond advertised capabilities
items.detail: checkProviderDouble covers the two capability flags the schema has today. It proves nothing about endpoints a row does not advertise, and it cannot detect a double that answers correctly but diverges from the real payload in a field no parser reads.
items.next_action: Extend the probe when a new capability flag or parser field is added; add a payload-shape comparison if a fixture divergence is observed.

items.title: First Fly deployment and first image build
items.detail: The packaging is committed, but no app, volume, secret or machine exists. fly apps create returns 'trial has ended, please add a credit card'. Docker's Linux engine cannot start on the development machine, so the first fly deploy will also be the image's first build. The 512 MB machine is an unmeasured cost point.
items.next_action: After the operator enables the Fly account and approves deployment under FID-2026-1030-062, run the five documented commands, confirm /api/ready, and record the image build and memory behavior.

items.title: Brand assets: texture source, logo weight and crawler crop
items.detail: assets/bg_pattern.jpg remains as the only source for bg-pattern.webp. logo.png is an 888 KB raster used at 36 px. No real crawler has been used, so platform crop and cache behavior for the 1200x630 card is unmeasured.
items.next_action: Delete the texture source only when it is redrawn; ship a 512 px square mark on the next logo change; test a real share when a public origin exists.

items.title: Per-page cards: crawler behavior, font coverage and /compare
items.detail: The card routes and tags are verified, but no crawler was used. Cards are Latin-only because next/og's default font has no CJK coverage, and /compare still inherits the site card.
items.next_action: Verify one real share per platform after a public origin exists; add a bundled CJK font if a non-Latin model name is published; revisit /compare only if its share volume justifies a per-query route.

items.title: Metadata gate coverage boundaries
items.detail: Slug-level legal pages use one representative each; /account, /admin/* and /dashboard are excluded as session-gated or noindex; the gate asserts tags and image serving, not platform cache or crop behavior.
items.next_action: Extend the representative set when a policy slug becomes a share surface; add a real-crawler check only if a public origin and a stable test target exist.

items.title: libSQL port revisit criteria
items.detail: FID-2026-1030-066 stays converged as the path back. D6 selected one persistent Node process on one local volume; the port reopens if the service must scale beyond one process or move to a host without same-host storage. The capability spike is scripts/libsql-capability-spike.mjs.
items.next_action: Re-run the settlement concurrency proof before any remote engine carries the ledger; do not port without that receipt.

items.title: Operator RPO/RTO and first hosted PostgreSQL restore
items.detail: The PostgreSQL backup/restore code and a disposable drill are verified (12/12 on 2026-11-02). No recovery-point or restore-time target is set, and no timed restore has run against the production-equivalent Neon Launch database. The 2026-10-31 Fly observation (apps list exit 1, no app/volume) still explains why no hosted target exists. The SQLite Fly-volume restore described in the archived FID is historical after the 2026-11-01 storage cutover.
items.next_action: Provision the Neon Launch project and the Fly app under FID-2026-1030-062/067, confirm the retention window, set the backup interval and restore target, run a timed restore of the production-equivalent PostgreSQL database, confirm /api/ready and /admin/reconciliation, and record the receipt.

items.title: Live provider reset and quota-refresh acceptance
items.detail: Parsing, freshness, reset, lease fencing and allocation are covered by tests/quota-refresh.test.mjs, tests/free-pool.test.mjs, tests/allocation.test.mjs and tests/trials.test.mjs. The real upstream reset boundary and the 15 rpm fallback under load were not exercised; the suite uses the mock provider.
items.next_action: On the next live provider pass, observe a UTC reset and a stale-observation refresh against the real account, record the used/remaining/reset values, and confirm admission refuses on failure rather than inventing capacity.

items.title: Hosted ingress, SIGTERM drain and first deployment acceptance
items.detail: The readiness code and disposable production start are verified. No Fly app, volume, machine or secret exists, so hosted proxy-header stripping, SSE flush/timeout/cancel, a live in-flight SIGTERM drain and the first deployment have not run. Final deployment approval remains FID-2026-1030-062.
items.next_action: After the operator enables the Fly account and approves deployment under 062, provision the app/volume, configure the trusted ingress header, and record the SSE/cancel, SIGTERM drain and readiness receipts against the pinned artifact.

items.title: Operator policy and support launch gates
items.detail: Policy v1.1 is published and the authenticated support queue is implemented. No registered entity/address, counsel review, verified host retention, Stripe business-profile/tax decision, real account deletion or controlled outside-channel inquiry exists yet.
items.next_action: Record each operator decision with its date, publish a new immutable policy version when text changes, and exercise one real deletion and one controlled inquiry through the owned channel.

items.title: Real payment and deployed-origin customer journey
items.detail: The 33-route, two-theme, 320/1024 matrix passes on a disposable production build (132/132). It is not a real payment: card top-ups are off by ruling and the NOWPayments sandbox/live smoke remains operator territory. No deployed origin exists, so the same matrix has not run against the public host.
items.next_action: After FID-062 approval and the FID-2026-1031-076 lane smoke, run one real top-up through the enabled lane and repeat the matrix against the deployed origin; record the payment state and the rendered account balance.

items.title: Operator alert destination, scheduler and received-alert receipt
items.detail: The monitor, HMAC-signed HTTPS transport, retry/dedup state and pause/drain/provider controls are verified against a local webhook receiver. No OPERATIONS_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL, signing secret, cron/Fly scheduler or external destination was configured, and no authorized alert has been received or responded to. The local suite is not proof of delivery to the operator.
items.next_action: After the operator selects a destination and supplies the URL (and optional 16+ character secret) outside the tree, install one scheduler run, trigger a controlled incident through the authenticated tick, record the received payload and HMAC verification, acknowledge/resolve it, and record the response action. Repeat against the hosted deployment after 062/067.

items.title: Operator-approved production envelope, real provider and PostgreSQL acceptance
items.detail: The 2026-10-31 run measured the production artifact on a disposable SQLite file and local provider fixture: 123/123 checks, 229.84 sustained rps, p95 137.53 ms, 186.7 MB peak RSS, 310 committed settlements and zero unresolved/ledger differences. Those numbers are SQLite-era and candidate-only. The gate is now PostgreSQL-native (FID-148), and a 2026-11-03 run against an isolated database in the configured Supabase cluster completed every workload with zero unresolved settlements and `integrity: ok`, but failed five candidate targets: 4.76 admitted rps against 20, steady p95 1,974 ms against 1,500 ms, ramp p95 2,211 ms, and two mixed-billing 503s. No real provider was called, no spend occurred, ENOSPC and 120 s/300 s deadline waits were not reproduced, and no hosted proxy was used. The envelope in config/load-envelope.json still has no dated approval; FID-062 item 5 remains open.
items.next_action: Close the five failed targets on a production-equivalent PostgreSQL host against the zero-spend mock provider fixture (funded-wallet testing was withdrawn by the operator on 2026-11-04; no provider spend is part of this gate), then date the operator traffic/spend envelope and run `npm run test:load:accept`; repeat with the hosted proxy and production-sized dataset, record ENOSPC/deadline behavior and publish only the approved cap.

items.title: Promo distribution and first customer redemption
items.detail: The promo lane is implemented and default-off. No code has been issued to a real customer, there is no delivery channel, and the operator has not decided whether promo dollars should ever expire. Unit and HTTP tests prove the local route, ledger transaction and concurrent redemption only.
items.next_action: Choose the recipient and distribution channel outside the app, enable PROMO_CODES_ENABLED only for the approved window, issue one code, record the customer redemption and ledger row, then close the flag.

items.title: Activity log retention, growth and export policy
items.detail: activity_events is append-only and metadata is bounded, but there is no retention job, export or customer-facing view. The table stores identifiers and amounts, not prompts or completions. No production-size growth measurement exists.
items.next_action: Before public volume, decide the retention window, add a pruning job if needed, and measure table growth under the approved load envelope.

items.title: Apixo zero-spend enablement, remaining cost entry and rate re-check
items.detail: On 2026-10-31 the operator supplied APIXOAI_API_KEY. The provider row adopted the documented variable name on restart and reports configured, was enabled, and synced 44 models with no warnings. All 43 models that appear on Apixo's public pricing page were costed and activated under the 2500-bps markup from a 2026-10-31 capture in docs/data/provider-prices.json; one synced id, glm5.3-flash-abliterated-backup, has no row on that page and stays disabled and unpublished. The capture also corrected qwen3-uncensored from a rounded 0.49/2.37 to the page's 0.4896/2.3664. The public catalog grew from 39 to 58 rows, with 25 published Apixo rows and 30 models served from Apixo, including takeovers of existing ids (gpt-6.1-sol, grok-4.7, free/mimo-v2.6-pro, glm-5.3 and others). Apixo exposes no balance or quota endpoint, so admission falls back to PROVIDER_SHARED_RPM and an unfunded wallet would fail those calls with no observable reserve. Funded-wallet testing was withdrawn by the operator on 2026-11-04; no funded call will be made and paid behavior against Apixo remains unverified.
items.next_action: Do not fund the wallet: funded-call acceptance was withdrawn on 2026-11-04. Before 2026-11-30 (PROVIDER_PRICE_MAX_AGE_DAYS) re-read https://apixoai.online/pricing and correct any captured rate that moved, because the cost is manual and the price window withholds the row once it ages out; the operator decides separately whether to keep the unfunded provider enabled.

items.title: PostgreSQL port landed; hosted Neon acceptance remains
items.detail: FID-085 and FID-086 are archived with 2026-11-01 closure bodies. The application resolves one PostgreSQL handle through lib/storage/runtime.ts; lib/db.ts and lib/store/* are deleted, better-sqlite3 is a devDependency for the one-way importer only, and npm run storage:check reports one storage engine. FID-066's libSQL target is retired. The remaining live obligations are a Neon Launch project, a hosted restore rehearsal and a PostgreSQL load rerun, which are tracked under FID-062 items 3, 5 and 7 and FID-058-LIVE/FID-060-LIVE.
items.next_action: Provision the Neon Launch project, confirm its retention window, run a hosted restore/rollback rehearsal and rerun the load envelope against PostgreSQL; record each dated receipt under FID-062 before approval.
